title: Morris USF Lab Protocol for Fictive Swallow Elicitation
author: Lauren Segers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bci8iuhw
materials: Various stimuli and perturbations were applied.

steps.title: Pre-surgical Preparation and Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Prepare adult cats for surgery using pharmacological agents and anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Inject atropine to reduce airway mucus secretion.
Administer dexamethasone to minimize brain stem swelling and prevent hypotension.
Induce anesthesia with 5.0% isoflurane and maintain with 1.0–3.0% isoflurane mixed with medical grade air until decerebration.

steps.title: Surgical Access and Monitoring Setup
steps.instruction: Establish intravenous access, airway management, and hemodynamic monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Intubate the trachea.
Place catheters in the femoral arteries and veins for drug/fluid administration and arterial blood pressure monitoring.
Periodically analyze arterial blood for PO2, PCO2, pH, and HCO3- concentrations.
Administer 8.4% sodium bicarbonate solution as needed to correct metabolic acidosis.
Administer 6% Hetastarch or 5% Dextran in half-normal saline and 0.04–0.1% dopamine in lactated Ringer solution intravenously as needed to maintain mean blood pressure ≥ 75 mmHg.

steps.title: Decerebration Procedure
steps.instruction: Perform decerebration to isolate the brainstem.

substeps.instruction: Ligate both external carotid arteries caudal to the lingual artery branch to reduce bleeding.
Administer an infusion of vecuronium bromide immediately prior to transection and maintain throughout the experiment to ensure paralysis.
Perform an occipital craniotomy, a midcollicular transection, and suction decerebration.
Gradually reduce isoflurane concentration to zero following decerebration.

steps.title: Neural Interface and Recording Setup
steps.instruction: Expose the brainstem and isolate peripheral nerves for recording and stimulation.

substeps.instruction: Remove the pia mater from the exposed brainstem and insert tungsten microelectrodes to measure neuron extracellular potentials.

Isolate and desheath the right hypoglossal (XII), left phrenic (Phr), left lumbar iliohypogastric (Lum), and right vagus (X) nerves (or right recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) instead of X in some subjects).
Place XII, Lum, and X/RLN nerves in coiled or hooked bipolar silver electrodes; cover with mineral oil and petroleum jelly, then wrap in parafilm.
Float the Phr nerve in a pool of mineral oil in a neck pocket, then section and record in coiled or hooked bipolar silver electrodes.
Isolate superior laryngeal nerves (SLNs) bilaterally, connect each to a silver bipolar electrode, and cover with mineral oil/petroleum jelly or a mineral oil-soaked pledget.
Configure signal processing: amplify, full-wave rectify, low-pass filter, and RC integrate (τ = 200–500 ms) all nerve activity.
Monitor integrated nerve activity, tracheal pressure, end tidal CO2, and arterial blood pressure via a Grass polygraph and record digitally.

steps.title: Fictive Swallow Elicitation Methods
steps.instruction: Apply various stimuli to evoke fictive swallowing, identified by changes in Phr, XII, and X/RLN nerve activities.

substeps.instruction: Electrical Stimulation: Stimulate SLN with pulse duration 0.1-0.25 ms, frequency 5–22 Hz, voltage 2.6–4.0 V, current 33.3–51.5 μA, and train duration 2–120 s.
Water Bolus: Rapidly inject 5–25 mL of water (less than 5 s) through a polyethylene tube in the mouth; perform at least 3 trials with ≥ 2 min inter-trial intervals.
Mechanical Stimulation: Insert and deliberately move the water tube.
Esophageal Balloon: Inflate a balloon inserted into the esophagus.

steps.title: Additional Physiological Stimulations
steps.instruction: Perform supplementary stimulations to observe respiratory and swallow responses.

substeps.instruction: Chemoreceptor Stimulation: Inject 1 ml of CO2-saturated saline over 30 s into the right carotid sinus (peripheral) or vertebral artery (central).
Blood Pressure Increase: Occlude the descending aorta with an embolectomy catheter for 30 s to increase mean arterial pressure by at least 25 mmHg.
Ventilator Manipulation: Delay or withhold lung inflation.
Nebulization: Nebulize AITC into the ventilator inspiratory line; administer Compound 48/80 if required.

steps.title: Ventilation Management
steps.instruction: Operate the ventilator using one of three modes.

substeps.instruction: Phrenic-triggered mode (PT): Use integrated phrenic signal to trigger inflation and allow passive deflation (mean delay between Phr peak and TP peak: 458 ± 140 ms).
Free-run mode (FR): Set rate to 30 breaths/min; adjust gas flow to maintain arterial PCO2 at 30 ± 0.5 mmHg.
A mode: Approximately double tidal volume and halve the rate to maintain PCO2 at 30-32 mmHg.

steps.title: Extracellular Neuronal Recording
steps.instruction: Acquire neuronal activity from the brainstem using multielectrode arrays.

substeps.instruction: Use three or four multielectrode arrays with high impedance tungsten microelectrodes (submicrometer adjustable steps).
Guide placement using anatomical landmarks (obex, brain stem midline), stereotaxic coordinates from Berman (1968), and previous literature.
Record from the dorsomedial medulla/nucleus of the solitary tract, ventral respiratory column, midline raphe nuclei/adjacent reticular formation, and lateral tegmental field-parafacial region.
Isolate single neuron waveforms using interactive spike sorting software.
Administer an overdose of Euthasol.
Monitor cardiac and respiratory activities until cessation.
